statement: Pisa and Genoa competed as rival maritime cities in the western Mediterranean, particularly for control of Corsica and Sardinia. The defining conflict was the Battle of Meloria (1284), in which a Genoese fleet decisively defeated the Pisan fleet; thousands of Pisan sailors were taken prisoner (they were kept in Genoa for years — the Genoese saying was 'to see Pisa, go to Genoa'). Meloria ended Pisa's status as a major naval power; Genoa took control of Corsica, and Pisa subsequently came under Florentine influence. Pisa's distinctive architectural achievements (Leaning Tower, baptistery) reflect the commercial wealth of its 11th–12th century prime.
